channel.title: Mihajlo Petrovic — Blog
channel.description: Software engineering, product thinking, and lessons learned from building real products.

item.title: Spec-Driven Development: The Antidote to Vibe Coding
item.description: When generating code takes minutes, the specification becomes the durable artifact and the code becomes an output. What a spec should contain, where it lives, and when vibe coding is still the right call.
item.author: mihajlop98@gmail.com (Mihajlo Petrovic)

item.title: AI Agents in Practice: BMAD, MCP, and SourceKit-LSP
item.description: A practical look at the plumbing around AI coding agents: the BMAD method for planning, MCP for tooling, and SourceKit-LSP for real Swift code intelligence - what each one does, how to set it up, and where it actually pays off.
item.author: mihajlop98@gmail.com (Mihajlo Petrovic)

item.title: Local LLMs on Apple Silicon: An Honest Verdict
item.description: How much RAM you actually need, what quantisation costs you, which tools are worth installing - and a clear answer on where a laptop model beats an API and where it is not remotely close.
item.author: mihajlop98@gmail.com (Mihajlo Petrovic)

item.title: AI in Regulated FinTech: The Engineering Constraints
item.description: What changes when the software is a bank's: data classification and residency, audit trails, the hard line between drafting and deciding, model upgrades as change management - and why internal developer tooling is where to start.
item.author: mihajlop98@gmail.com (Mihajlo Petrovic)

item.title: AI Code Review: What It Catches and What It Misses
item.description: An honest breakdown of where an AI reviewer genuinely outperforms a tired human, where it is blind by construction, and the three configuration mistakes that make a team mute the bot in week two.
item.author: mihajlop98@gmail.com (Mihajlo Petrovic)

item.title: Evals: How to Test a Feature That Never Gives the Same Answer Twice
item.description: You cannot unit-test an LLM feature, so most teams ship prompt changes on vibes and break things silently. How to build a golden set, assert cheaply before reaching for a judge model, and wire it all into CI.
item.author: mihajlop98@gmail.com (Mihajlo Petrovic)

item.title: Shipping an LLM Feature in an Angular App
item.description: Prototyping an AI feature takes an afternoon; shipping one takes longer, and almost none of the extra time is prompting. Streaming with SSE, cancellation, rate limits, caching and cost control - with the Angular and Node code.
item.author: mihajlop98@gmail.com (Mihajlo Petrovic)

item.title: SwiftUI for Angular Developers: A Practical Guide
item.description: Coming to SwiftUI from Angular, the concepts map more cleanly than you expect - and the places they do not map are exactly where you lose a week. Here is what transfers, what traps you, and how to pick the right state wrapper the first time.
item.author: mihajlop98@gmail.com (Mihajlo Petrovic)

item.title: RAG vs Long Context: Do You Actually Need a Vector Database?
item.description: Million-token context windows and prompt caching changed the maths. How to tell whether your corpus needs a real retrieval pipeline or just needs to be pasted into the prompt - and how to build retrieval properly if it does.
item.author: mihajlop98@gmail.com (Mihajlo Petrovic)

item.title: My Daily AI Workflow in the Terminal
item.description: No chat window, no magic - a concrete account of how I actually use coding agents day to day: instructions files, plan-first prompting, sub-agents, hooks, worktrees, and the things I deliberately never delegate.
item.author: mihajlop98@gmail.com (Mihajlo Petrovic)

item.title: Building Your First MCP Server
item.description: MCP lets you write one integration that any AI client can use. A minimal working server in TypeScript, plus the design lessons that only show up after you have built one badly.
item.author: mihajlop98@gmail.com (Mihajlo Petrovic)

item.title: Context Engineering: Why Your AI Agent Forgets What You Told It
item.description: Agents do not get worse over a long session - their context does. What actually fills a context window, why quality degrades before you hit the limit, and five habits that make the model noticeably smarter for free.
item.author: mihajlop98@gmail.com (Mihajlo Petrovic)

item.title: About Me — From Code to Career
item.description: A personal introduction to who I am, how I got into software engineering, and what drives me every day as a developer.
item.author: mihajlop98@gmail.com (Mihajlo Petrovic)

item.title: Why I Chose Angular in 2024 (and Still Use It)
item.description: React gets all the hype, but Angular is the framework I keep coming back to. Here's why I think it's underrated for serious applications.
item.author: mihajlop98@gmail.com (Mihajlo Petrovic)

item.title: Building Banking Software: Lessons from the Trenches
item.description: Working in FinTech has taught me things no tutorial ever could. Here are my honest lessons from building software that handles real people's money.
item.author: mihajlop98@gmail.com (Mihajlo Petrovic)
